samples.summary: v1 PATCH /documents/:id takes an unvalidated inline body while an equivalent validated DTO exists, so a non-string `folderId` reaches Prisma as a 500 and a blank/over-long title is accepted
samples.evidence: `@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null }` is an inline object type, so the global `ValidationPipe` (main.ts:66, `whitelist`/`forbidNonWhitelisted`) skips it entirely (no metatype to validate). The new move path then feeds the raw value straight into Prisma: `folderId: 5` or `folderId: {}` passes `body.folderId !== undefined && !== null` and reaches `this.folderService.assertSameWorkspace(body.folderId, workspaceId)` → `prisma.folder.findUnique({ where: { id: <number|object> } })` → `PrismaClientValidationError`, an unhandled 500 rather than a 400. Likewise `title: null` sets `data.title = null` on a non-nullable column (500), and `title: ''` / a 10k-char title is stored, whereas the web sibling `DocumentController.updateDocument` (document.controller.ts:314) binds the very same fields through `UpdateDocumentDto` (document.dto.ts:92-106) with `@IsString() @Length(1,200)` and `@IsUUID()`. The new v1 folders controller does use DTOs (`CreateFolderDto`/`UpdateFolderDto`), so this is the one new write surface without validation. Title looseness is pre-existing; the `folderId` crash path is added by this change.

samples.summary: Folder delete is gated on the *top* folder's author only, but the DB cascade destroys every descendant folder, including ones authored by other users
samples.evidence: `remove` checks `isManager(folder, req)` for the named folder alone, then calls `folderService.delete(folderId)`. The schema declares `Folder_parentId_fkey ... ON DELETE CASCADE` (prisma/migrations/20260719142600_add_workspace_folders/migration.sql:29), so a plain member who authored one folder can permanently delete the whole subtree beneath it — subfolders created by the workspace owner or other members — with no check against those rows. Documents survive (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), so this is loss of folder structure rather than content, and it mirrors the pre-existing web `FolderController.remove` (folder.controller.ts:113). This change is what makes it reachable from an API key / CLI, where it is trivially scriptable.

samples.summary: New API-key membership check does `Number(user.id)` on an `id` the local type marks optional, turning a malformed key principal into a Prisma 500 instead of a 403
samples.evidence: `AuthUser` (image-read.controller.ts:21-25) declares `id?: number | string`, and the new branch calls `this.workspaceService.assertMember(resolvedWorkspaceId, Number(user.id))` without checking `user.id !== undefined` — the way the JWT branch immediately below it does (`if (user?.id !== undefined)`). With `id` absent, `Number(undefined)` is `NaN` and `prisma.workspaceMember.findUnique({ where: { workspaceId_userId: { workspaceId, userId: NaN } } })` raises a Prisma validation error, surfacing as an unhandled 500 rather than the intended 403. `ApiKeyStrategy.validate` does always set `id: apiKey.createdBy`, so this is defensive today; it is only reachable if another api-key principal shape is ever introduced.

samples.summary: `folders delete` help text says only that documents return to the root, omitting that descendant folders are deleted
samples.evidence: The description reads 'Delete a folder; its documents return to the workspace root (never deleted)', which reads as non-destructive, but the DB cascade (`Folder_parentId_fkey ... ON DELETE CASCADE`) removes every descendant folder too. The schema registry entry for the same command does say 'Delete a folder and its descendant folders' (packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts), so the two descriptions an agent may read disagree on the blast radius of a destructive command.
searchedFor: prisma migration for Folder parent FK

samples.summary: `--dry-run` skips `--format` validation in the new rename/move/delete and docs copy/move handlers but not in the new list/create ones
samples.evidence: In `folders list` and `folders create` `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` runs before the `opts.dryRun` branch; in `folders rename`, `folders move`, `folders delete`, `docs copy` and `docs move` it runs after, so `--dry-run --format bogus` prints a preview instead of the format error the sibling commands raise. The repo states the intended rule explicitly in docs.ts:82 ('Parsed BEFORE the dry-run branch: `--dry-run` validates inputs'). Cosmetic — the preview is JSON regardless — but the new file is internally inconsistent about it.
